To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the African honey bee forages in small areas and visits few sites when foraging resources are abundant.

(1) foraging ranges of colonies are small, (2) foraging ranges are correlated with brood rearing during times of resource abundance, (3) during periods of resource abundance, colonies are able to adjust their foraging patterns in response to changes in brood reing, and (4) during times of resource dearth colonies are unable to coordinate foraging with changes in brood production.
foraging patterns are correlated with colony energy levels only during periods of relative resource abundance.

the spatial and temporal patterns of foraging by the African honey bee and how foraging patterns change in response to changes in the availability of floral food resources.
